title: Third-Party Shelf Launch Playbook & Localization Checklist (Draft)
content:
Purpose:

This doc is a working playbook for launching third-party partner tiles on the cloud shelf (public vendor gallery). It combines product copy drafts, operational acceptance gates, localization guidance, and a lightweight rollout plan for pilots and wider GA. Use this as the canonical preflight for a tile to be published to Azure/GCP marketplaces and the Redwood cloud shelf.

Audience:
- GTM launch manager (owner)
- Partner PM/engineer (publisher)
- Legal/compliance reviewer
- Billing & entitlements
- Localization lead / i18n engineer

High-level launch flow (phases):
1) Intake & eligibility (owner: GTM intake)
   - Partner intake form submitted (JIRA J-PL-889).
   - Quick eligibility check: supported regions, model licensing, data residency concerns.
   - Decide pilot geography and pricing band.
2) Copy + creative prep (owner: content + partner)
   - Draft tile name, 20-word elevator, 3 feature bullets, short use-case example.
   - Acquire 1 hero screenshot and 1 short demo gif (1280x720).
   - Accessibility alt text for images.
3) Technical acceptance (owner: platform eng)
   - Verify API contract compatibility (token auth, CORS, endpoint SLA).
   - Confirm telemetry hooks (tile_id, region, plan) and logging retention.
   - Smoke test provisioning flow (trial entitlement + billing seat).
4) Legal & security (owner: legal/security)
   - Confirm license terms for bundled models (OSS license scan).
   - Confirm PII handling and data residency if required.
   - Ensure indemnities and branding guidelines passed.
5) Localization & i18n checklist (owner: localization lead)
   - Translate tile title, elevator, bullets into target locales (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP).
   - Ensure character limits per marketplace tile (see marketplace copy guide).
   - Localize screenshots and demo copy where required.
6) Billing & SKU mapping (owner: finance ops)
   - Map partner plans to marketplace SKUs and Redwood billing product codes.
   - Validate trial duration, quotas, and overage rules.
7) Launch staging and QA (owner: QA)
   - Publish to staging shelf, run end-to-end checkout and provisioning.
   - Telemetry verification, A/B fallback checks.
8) Canary & GA rollout (owner: GTM)
   - 1-week canary in pilot region, monitor errors and conversion.
   - GA with regional ramp and docs page published.

Acceptance checklist (checkbox style; fill before approving):
- [ ] Product tile title (<= 60 chars) drafted and approved
- [ ] 20-word elevator pitch drafted
- [ ] 3 concise feature bullets (each <= 140 chars)
- [ ] Example use case + recommended prompt templates
- [ ] Hero image and alt text uploaded
- [ ] Demo GIF (<= 10s) uploaded
- [ ] Accessibility quick review passed
- [ ] API contract documented (endpoint, auth, latency SLO)
- [ ] KV cache and batching guidance included for partners with heavy token usage
- [ ] Telemetry keys instrumented and tested
- [ ] Billing SKU mapping validated with Finance
- [ ] Trial entitlement flow tested end-to-end
- [ ] Legal sign-off on licenses and branding
- [ ] Security review (SAST/DAST summary) complete
- [ ] I18n translations (requested locales) uploaded
- [ ] Marketplace-specific character/format constraints validated
- [ ] Staging publish and QA smoke test passed
- [ ] Rollout plan and rollback steps documented

Localization granular notes (practical):
- Character limits: Azure tile title 60 chars; GCP short description 110 chars; consolidate to shortest limit to avoid truncation.
- Date/time formats: use locale-specific short formats in screenshots/demo.
- Currency & price formatting: avoid hardcoding currency in tile copy; use marketplace metadata instead.
- Contact strings: use localized support URLs and phone numbers where available.
- Avoid idioms and US-centric metaphors in elevator text; keep neutral.

Copy snippets (do not finalise — partner must approve):
- Tile title (draft): "Redwood + Acme: Real-time Semantic Search"
- 20-word elevator (draft): "Deploy Acme’s domain-tuned embeddings on Redwood’s inference runtime for low-latency semantic search across private datasets."
- Feature bullets (draft):
  - "Plug-and-play embeddings with prebuilt connectors to S3, BigQuery, and Postgres."
  - "Low-latency vector search with automatic quantization and cost controls."
  - "Enterprise-ready: VPC support, audit logs, and SOC2 controls."
- Example use case snippet (for tile details):
  - "Customer support teams reduce average time-to-resolution by surfacing relevant KB articles via semantic search — sample prompt and CSV connector config included."

Operational edge cases and mitigations:
- Geo-limited models: if partner model cannot be served in target region, fallback to smaller regional variant and mark on tile as "Region-limited (see docs)".
- Unexpected cost spikes: enforce soft quota on trials and require partner approval for quota increases.
- Failed entitlements: rollback to trial-disabled state and notify partner and ops.

QA test plan (smoke tests):
- Create trial, verify provisioning completes within SLA (<= 90s).
- Confirm sample query returns expected schema and no PII leakage (sanity check).
- Simulate 5 concurrent sessions to ensure autoscaler keeps latency < 500ms for 512-token requests.
- Verify telemetry events: tile_view, purchase_start, purchase_complete, trial_expiry.

Owners & timeline (example pilot):
- Week 0: Intake + eligibility (Priya / Partner PM)
- Week 1: Copy + creative (Content / Partner)
- Week 2: Technical acceptance + Billing mapping (Platform Eng / Finance)
- Week 3: Localization + Legal review (Localization / Legal)
- Week 4: Staging publish + QA (QA / Priya)
- Week 5: Canary (pilot region)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm whether partner requires co-branding assets in all locales.
- Decide archival policy for demo data used in screenshots.
- Confirm if partner wants a direct signup flow or redirect to partner-managed consent page.
- Get final marketplace tile size spec for new GCP UI update (P0 if changed).

Appendix: Links & references
- Confluence: Partner shelf publisher guide (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: Launch epic J-PL-889
- GitHub: tile templates and example (github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-tiles)
- Slack: #marketplace-launch for async questions

Quick owner checklist (one-liners to tick in standups):
- Intake form done? -> J-PL-889 created
- Draft copy shipped to partner? -> ask for approval + translation list
- Images optimized? -> confirm sizes and alt text included
- Billing mapped? -> finance sign-off
- Legal sign-off? -> block for legal if not done

End of draft.

Note: This is an iterative working doc — share edits in the slack thread linked above. Final publishing must be run through the Marketplace publishing runbook before GA.
